title: 用 osFoundry Operator 讓 AI 代理操作 App，每個動作都留下紀錄
summary:
「我的 GPU endpoint 有哪些還在計費？」這個問題很簡單，但要回答它，通常得點進三個畫面、讀出數字，再回到聊天視窗把它們打出來。把這件事交給 AI 代理聽起來很不錯，直到你開始追問：它到底點了什麼？osFoundry Operator 就是圍繞這個問題設計的：代理在對話旁邊的 App 即時窗格裡工作，它做的每個動作都會被記錄下來。

對話旁邊，就是 App 的即時窗格

osFoundry 是一款把聊天、代理、檔案和工具整合在同一個視窗裡的桌面 App。Operator 把畫面分成三欄。左邊是 Operator 的工作階段清單，中間是對話，右邊則是即時的 dashboard 窗格：一份真正的 osFoundry App，Operator 會在裡面開啟各個畫面。窗格上方會顯示目前所在的畫面（這裡是 Dashboard /models/endpoints），並提供 Home 與 Project 捷徑、Reload dashboard 和 Open in a new window。拖曳分隔線就能把窗格拉寬。

summary:

title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
summary:
Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions.

They're too good at describing the work

The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb.

It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop!

title: Podcast: Distributed LLM Inference on Kubernetes with llm-d, Wasm, & TornadoVM
summary:
In this episode, Edoardo Vacchi discusses the evolving landscape of WebAssembly on the backend, running Java workloads on GPUs using TornadoVM, and optimizing distributed AI inference using llm-d and vLLM on Kubernetes. Edoardo explains how llm-d manages cache locality (KV and prefix caches), request routing, and batch inference across Kubernetes clusters to maximize expensive GPU utilization.

By Edoardo Vacchi

title: Article: Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
summary:
Agentic AI architecture extends microservices and cloud-native architectures with AI agents that work with context, memory, and protocols such as MCP and A2A. The article covers bounded-context integration, task-dependent coordination strategies, new security risks, and observability needs. It expects gradual adoption alongside existing architectures, with platforms absorbing common components.

By Rafał Gancarz

title: A job offer on LinkedIn came with malware in a Git hook. It's the "Contagious Interview" playbook
summary:
A recruiter messaged me on LinkedIn about building the website for a blockchain basketball game. Then they sent a documentation pack as a .tar.gz file. The plan was simple: review the docs, sign the NDA, then we'd schedule a call.

The docs were real enough to read. The archive also held a Git hook that would have downloaded a script and run it on my Mac the first time I checked out a branch. One of its branches was called NDA.

It follows the playbook of a campaign security researchers have been tracking for a while, called Contagious Interview: fake recruiters, web3 projects, and code that runs when a developer does something routine. With so many developers looking for work right now, I'm writing up exactly what it looked like, so it's easier to spot. title: Seven Tests I Write Before I Trust a .NET Play Counter
summary:
A play counter is the easiest feature to demo and one of the easiest to get quietly wrong. plays = plays + 1 passes every manual test you'll ever click through. It also counts a retried request four times, loses plays when a worker crashes at the wrong moment, and happily lets one script "listen" to a track 2,000 times an hour.

So when I built a Spotify-style play count in .NET 10 recently, I didn't start with the counter. I started with the tests that would tell me the counter was lying. title: An Empty Role Can Make a Salary Tool Confidently Wrong
summary:
Your weekend agent can forget roles, get a plausible salary back, and confidently answer your question about a different job. Nothing crashes. That's the annoying part.

In salaryBenchmarks, an empty roles value selects a default accounting role. The adapter examples below are synthetic: they demonstrate a validation boundary, not salary accuracy.

Lab note 077: can we reject a missing subject before a helpful fallback turns it into an answer?

How does a missing role pass validation?

The Actor has 41 input properties and 5 mode values, but only mode is required. A salary request can therefore satisfy the input schema without specifying whose salary you wanted.

That makes execution success a weak signal. It tells your agent that a lookup completed, not that the lookup concerned the user's role.

title: What I Check Before Trusting a Digital Product Automation Workflow
summary:
Getting an automation workflow to run is one thing.

Trusting it to handle real orders is another.

When you connect Payhip, Make, Telegram, and Notion, it's easy to focus on whether all the tools are connected. But a successful test doesn't necessarily mean the workflow is ready to handle real customers.

There are a few things worth checking before relying on it.

Here is the checklist I use when thinking about a digital product order workflow.

1. Check whether the payment event is received correctly

The workflow starts with a purchase event from Payhip.

Before moving on, check:

  • Does Make receive the expected event?
  • Is the correct product identified?
  • Is the order reference available?
  • Does the workflow distinguish a successful purchase from other events?

Don't assume that a connected webhook means everything is working correctly.
